rationale: Coaching is voluntary and already offered, so the honest design is a prospective observational comparison over one academic year: every resident films the same index operation at the start and end, two consultants who do not coach that resident rate edited videos blind (c2), and the analysis adjusts for baseline score and training year because residents who choose coaching differ (c1). Videos are kept out of assessment (c3).
alternatives: Randomised allocation to coaching or no coaching (refused: coaching is already offered, 14 residents are too few, and residents would not accept being denied it)
Before-after comparison of the whole programme (refused: cannot separate coaching from ordinary progression through training)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial across several programmes would be needed for a precise effect; this study gives the local estimate and the measurement experience such a trial would need.

decision.statement: Run a prospective observational comparison of coached and uncoached residents over the 2027 to 2028 academic year, with the change in blinded global rating scale score of an edited laparoscopic cholecystectomy video as the primary outcome.
decision.question: How should the programme find out whether video review coaching improves residents' operative skill?

criteria.text: Skill change can be measured reliably by blinded rating of edited videos, and a comparison of coached and uncoached residents has shown a plausible difference.
Fewer than four residents decline coaching, leaving no usable comparison group.

gates.requirement: Programme director agreement to use training videos for research and to keep them out of assessment
Research ethics board decision on a study of residents as participants

alternatives: Before-after comparison of the whole programme
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3; no local fact yet shows either gate met.

summary: Prospective observational comparison recommended; both gates are unknown until the investigator supplies approvals.
